title: Checksum-guided calibration for preserving structured response fidelity under FP8/INT8
creator: Ava Morales
description: Goal: Build and validate a checksum-guided calibration workflow that reduces silent structured-output regressions (JSON schema mismatches, missing/extra keys, type deviations) when models are quantized to FP8/INT8. The approach augments numeric calibration with deterministic token-level checksums computed over canonical serializations of expected structured outputs. We will use these checksums as lightweight invariants during calibration and post-deploy canarying to detect regressions quickly without full schema parsing for every request. The outcome should be: improved detection of schema-breaking regressions, fewer false positives from harmless tokenization variations, and a calibration loop that can recommend per-layer quant settings or fallbacks when checksums degrade beyond thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end calibration run produces checksum stability metrics for 95% of golden prompt set samples under FP8 and INT8 profiles
Automated canary detects schema-mismatch class regressions within 5 minutes of deploy for 90% of injected faults
No more than 1% increase in end-to-end latency at serving time from checksum computation when enabled in lightweight mode
Calibration tool outputs suggested layer-level quant adjustments or automatic fallback to higher-precision variant when checksum delta exceeds threshold
test_plan: Create golden prompt set (2k prompts) with structured outputs covering nested objects, arrays, optional fields, and enums
Instrument calibration harness to compute CRC32 and SHA1 of canonical JSON (stable key ordering, whitespace normalized) for each sample
Run grid of quant profiles (baseline float32, FP8 variants, INT8 symmetric/asymmetric) and capture checksum deltas and schema-assertion pass rates
Simulate production canary: deploy quantized variant to 1% traffic and verify canary pipeline flags regression within 5 minutes after injecting synthetic schema-breaking perturbations
Add unit tests for canonicalization logic and fuzz tests for tokenization-induced formatting variations
notes: Design trade-off: using checksums is cheaper than full JSON schema validation at scale but requires strict canonicalization to avoid false positives due to deterministic formatting differences
We prefer CRC32 for fast online checks and SHA1 in offline calibration reports to group failure clusters
Edge case: semantic-equivalent re-ordering of map fields will break checksum unless canonicalization sorts keys; we will canonicalize using stable key ordering defined in the spec
Decision: checksum module will be implemented as a small C++ extension for the runtime hot path, with a fallback Python implementation for offline tooling
Privacy: checksums are one-way and will not leak payload content, but we will treat any checksum-derived telemetry as potentially sensitive and follow existing PII telemetry rules
steps: Finalize canonical JSON spec and implement reference canonicalizer
Prototype checksum collector in offline calibration harness and run baseline profiles
Integrate fast CRC32 checksum into runtime as opt-in lightweight guard
Add canary pipeline hook and alert rules based on checksum delta percentiles
Roll out to dedicated capacity canaries, monitor false-positive rate for 2 weeks, iterate
review_feedback: PM: add acceptance criteria that ties to user-facing error rates and SLAs (not just internal metrics)
Design: please include examples of canonicalization rules in the design doc; watch out for locale-specific number formatting
Security: telemetry must be hashed and access-controlled; confirm no raw payload leakage
Infra: include revert plan; if checksum module causes perf regressions enable kill-switch via config
